## Summary
- `resources/lang/nl/validation.php` only had the 21 custom keys the app itself introduced (`form-has-errors`, `verplicht`, `tussen`, ...); none of Laravel's standard rule keys existed, so any field not covered by a `FormRequest::messages()` override fell back to the framework's English default even with `app.locale` on `nl`. `VehicleForm::save()` (the vehicle sheet) never overrides `messages()` at all, so every field on it was affected — e.g. an empty mileage rendered "The mileage field is required."
- Added the full Laravel 12 standard rule set to `nl`, `fr`, `de` and `en` (the English default file was itself missing several newer rules like `enum`, `prohibited_if`, `multiple_of`). The 21 pre-existing short keys (`max`, `min`, `numeric`, ...) are left untouched — those are called directly from `messages()` overrides elsewhere and changing them would touch already-working screens.
- Added an `attributes` array to each locale so `:attribute` renders a real field name instead of the raw column: derived from `VehicleForm::fieldLabels()` for the vehicle sheet, and from the `rules()` of the order/offer/relation/settings requests for the rest.
- `es` ships as a language file for the rest of the app, but `SetLangMiddleware` never lists `es` among its supported locales, so a dealer can never actually select it — left out of this pass; noted in the finding file.

## Test plan
- [x] New `tests/Feature/ValidationLanguageTest.php`: `VehicleForm::save()` with an empty mileage now renders "Het veld kilometerstand is verplicht."; an uncovered `in:` rule on the order form renders "Het geselecteerde garantietype is ongeldig."; `fr`/`de` also render in their own language.
- [x] `vendor/bin/phpunit --filter "Validation|VehicleForm|Order|RulesCoverage|RulesIdentity"` — 89 tests, all green.
- [x] `vendor/bin/phpunit --filter "AlpineExpressionTest|HandlerWiringTest|CompiledViewsTest|StylesheetSyntaxTest"` — 11 tests, all green.
- [x] Finding logged: `docs/bedrijfsregels/bevindingen/2026-09-15-validatiefouten-in-het-engels.md` (opgelost).
